mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: A plate always dries completely before a bottle cap, even if the plate holds much more water.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: With temperature and exposed area equal, water evaporates faster in humid air than in dry air.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: At the same temperature and humidity, the same amount of water evaporates faster in a large narrow-necked bottle than in a small shallow saucer because the bottle is bigger.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: Water at 30°C cannot evaporate; it must reach its boiling point.

intelligence.enrichment: Water evaporates faster when more surface is exposed to air, when it is warmer or in sunlight, and when air has less water vapour; it evaporates slower in humid air. Changing exposed area, warmth, sunlight, air movement, or humidity changes the time taken for water to evaporate. The learner correctly applies this rule: Water evaporates faster when more surface is exposed to air, when it is warmer or in sunlight, and when air has less water vapour; it evaporates slower in humid air. Only the amount of water controls evaporation time; exposed area, sunlight, wind, and humidity do not matter.
